No bond price, yield or spread on a dated trading day is supplied. The third-quarter report prints period-end fair values for the three senior note series, estimated from quoted market prices, which gives a quarter-end price level but not a trade date, yield or spread; Market-implied risk and Security selection work are limited to that. This is a minor gap for the requested work. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10
No portfolio, mandate or exposure data is supplied, so Committee decision work states the fund's limits as not supplied and portfolio fit is not established. This is a minor gap.

The filings define adjusted EBIT, reconciled by segment, but no adjusted EBITDA, no company-defined net leverage, no management guidance, and no earnings release or investor presentation is supplied, so any EBITDA or leverage measure is built by the analyst from the statements and is not a company-reported figure. This is a minor gap. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66

Stand-alone quarterly reports for 2025 are not supplied. The 2025 quarters are available as comparatives inside the 2026 reports, but the fourth quarter of 2025 exists only as the annual figure less nine months, and no discrete quarter of 2024 can be built because the 2024 interim reports are absent. This is a minor gap. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 102–104

Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

The issuer states no EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated for every period and adjusted EBITDA, the adjusted leverage and cover ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied. This restricts comparison with covenant EBITDA and with issuer-adjusted leverage. Severity: Medium. The action that would close it is the credit agreement definition of EBITDA or an earnings release that states one. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66

Lines the filings print as a dash are Not supplied rather than zero: loss on early extinguishment of debt in the periods without one, equity in earnings of affiliates in FY2023, the purchase of business in FY2023 and FY2025, proceeds from issuance of long-term debt in the nine months of 2026, debt issuance costs in FY2023 and the first half of 2025, and net sales of corporate and eliminations. Interim statements do not print deferred income taxes, the purchase of business or, for the first quarter and half year, proceeds from issuance of long-term debt, so those cells are Not supplied. These cells restrict nothing in the ratios. Severity: Low. No action is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 102–104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4

The balance sheet prints no total liabilities line, so Total Liabilities is calculated from the printed lines and agrees with assets less equity in every column; discrete second- and third-quarter depreciation and amortization is derived by difference because only year-to-date figures are printed; the fourth quarter of 2025 is calculated as the full year less nine months because no fourth quarter is reported. Severity: Low. The fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close the last of these. Basis: calculation C28; calculation C4; calculation C54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

The 2023 revolver commitment and letters of credit are not printed in the supplied filings, although no revolving loans were outstanding at the end of 2023, so undrawn committed facilities for FY2023 is Not supplied and the liquidity series starts at FY2024. Undrawn committed facilities is the revolver only; other foreign facilities are not quantified. Severity: Medium for the liquidity series. The action is the 2023 annual report and facility-level availability. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

Euro-denominated principal at September 30, 2026 is not printed for the euro term loans, and the filing prints only US dollar translations for the 2028 and 2031 euro notes, so the debt instrument table shows the translations as the amount in the reporting currency, with the euro principal Not supplied for the term loans and taken from the issue amount in the annual report for the notes; no rate is applied. Severity: Low. The action is the 2026 annual report note. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–124

Other foreign bank revolving and term loans and finance leases, together USD 88.978 million, state no ranking or security, so they are left out of the debt stack and the cumulative leverage excludes them. Severity: Low. The action is the underlying loan terms. Basis: calculation C65; calculation C66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8

The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025 and predates the 2026 prepayment of USD 42.5 million of term loans and the repayment of the USD 500.0 million secured notes, and no ladder at September 30, 2026 is supplied. Severity: Medium. The action is the 2026 annual report ladder or a lender schedule. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9

Last-twelve-months leverage at September 30, 2025 is not calculable because nine months of 2024 are not supplied, so no year-on-year comparison of trailing leverage at the same seasonal date is possible. Severity: Low. The action is the 2025 quarterly reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

The pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on net debt and net leverage is not established: the filing states no net debt effect, no sources and uses and no pro forma balance sheet, and the post-balance-sheet table therefore carries Not supplied figures. Severity: High. The action is the transaction agreements and pro forma financial information. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

Covenant levels, reported covenant ratios and the credit agreement definitions of Total Net Leverage and Interest Coverage are not printed, so covenant headroom cannot be stated and the ratios here are on this module's own definitions. Severity: High for covenant work. The action is the credit agreement and compliance certificates. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

Funds from operations is not defined in the filings or in the method, so funds from operations over total debt is Not calculable. Severity: Low. The action is an analyst definition agreed with the reader. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104

The annual report discussion prints total adjusted EBIT for FY2023 as 660.5 in millions while the note prints 660,553 in thousands, a rounding difference in the sum of rounded segment figures; the note figure is used. Severity: Low. No action is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is diversified across three packaging segments and anchored by contracts that pass raw-material cost through, which gives creditors more cash-flow visibility than a single-product packager would. Metal Containers was 48.4% of 2025 net sales, Dispensing and Specialty Closures 41.8% and Custom Containers 9.8%; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year arrangements, metal costs pass through by contract and resin costs pass through with a lag in many cases. The other side is a thin metal margin: Metal Containers earned an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025 against 15.5% in Dispensing and Specialty Closures. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 17, 21–22, 66–68; calculation A1

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Underlying 2026 operating momentum is weaker than the sales line suggests. Nine-month net sales rose 4.6%, mostly from cost pass-through and currency, while unit volumes fell in all three segments and adjusted EBIT was flat at USD 572.2 million against USD 572.6 million. An inventory program liquidated older LIFO layers and cut cost of goods sold by USD 34.0 million in the nine months, USD 26.8 million of it in the third quarter; if the whole benefit sits in adjusted EBIT, the measure would have been 6.01% below the prior-year nine months and 5.97% below the prior-year quarter without it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15–16, 18–20, 22–23; calculation A13; calculation A14

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The announced perimeter takes the largest segment by sales, and a large share of earnings, out of the direct reach of Silgan's existing creditors. Metal Containers contributed 36.0% of 2025 adjusted EBIT and 38.60% in the first nine months of 2026, and the perimeter also includes a flat cap closures business whose size is not stated. Silgan would own 60% of the partnership and consolidate it, but the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and USD 1.0 billion secured revolver would be secured by the partnership's assets only, and the other 40% would belong to an investment vehicle affiliated with American Industrial Partners that contributes about USD 1.0 billion of cash. Unless existing guarantees and share pledges continue to cover the contributed subsidiaries, which the note does not say, existing creditors of the parent would reach those assets only through the 60% interest, after the partnership's own lenders. The partnership would also buy Trivium, which the 2025 annual report names among the most significant metal container competitors, so the combination adds scale in the segment that already carries the largest customer concentration and depends on regulatory approval. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation A2; calculation A3

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The senior notes now rest on the parent alone while the bank debt keeps subsidiary support. The U.S. subsidiaries' guarantees of the three unsecured senior note series, USD 1,849.38 million of principal and 40.54% of total debt at September 30, 2026, fell away automatically on March 31, 2026 when the secured 1.4% notes were repaid, and the filings print no replacement guarantor. The Credit Agreement, 57.51% of debt principal, stays guaranteed by the U.S. subsidiaries and a Dutch borrower subsidiary and is supported by pledges of subsidiary shares, so noteholders sit behind subsidiary-level claims, and the partnership's secured lenders would add another layer ahead of them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 118, 122–124; calculation A10

facts.text: Governance is conventional and the audit record is clean, but the control picture is incomplete. Director independence, compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement is listed but not supplied, so the sponsor and governance risk read is medium and provisional. facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the announced transaction, if completed as described, would pay down about half of the group's debt: the USD 2.3 billion cash distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, and Silgan would keep control and full consolidation of the segment. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Executed agreements and a pro forma capital structure would settle the largest open question: which debt is retired, whether the Trivium debt is refinanced or stays in place, and whether the partnership's lenders have any recourse to Silgan. Which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or unsecured notes. Evidence of a large founder or fund holder, or terms in the 2022 stockholders agreement that bind the board, would move the governance read from conventional to influenced. A debt-funded dividend or repurchase after the transaction, loss or repricing of the Nestlé agreement, or a second year of volume declines without pass-through offsets would move the view the other way. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 98

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The partnership would also acquire Trivium Packaging B.V., a Netherlands supplier of metal packaging, for a cash payment of about USD 327.5 million and the assumption of about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium's debt. Trivium is one of the competitors that the 2025 annual report names among the most significant in metal containers. Closing is expected in mid-2027 and is subject to regulatory approvals, works council consultation and customary conditions. Costs attributed to announced acquisitions were USD 10.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, against USD 1.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, and adjusted EBIT excludes them; the filing does not tie them to a named transaction. The note gives no agreement terms, no sources and uses, no pro forma balance sheet and no separate figures for the flat cap closures business; the stated cash sources of USD 5.9 billion exceed the stated cash uses of USD 2.3 billion to Silgan and USD 327.5 million to Trivium's sellers by about USD 3.27 billion, close to the USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt, which is consistent with refinancing that debt but does not establish it. facts.text: Silgan issued no notes or term loans in the first nine months of 2026. facts.label: T2D.9 - Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by a stated policy of using leverage for growth and shareholder returns and by the unquantified Silgan MCC transaction, because that policy allows debt to rise again after any paydown and the transaction changes claim ranking, which implies refinancing and monitoring exposure. Countervailing evidence is the record of early refinancing, no waivers, no liability management exchange and a conventional board with a separate chair. Further analysis requires the transaction agreements, the proxy statement and the executed credit agreement.

facts.text: The business supports the debt through contract-backed, cost-pass-through earnings rather than growth. Reported EBITDA margins stayed between 13.51% and 14.34% from 2023 to 2025 even though EBITDA fell 7.88% in 2024; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year contracts that pass metal cost through, while resin cost passes through with a lag. The price is thin metal margins, an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025, and one concentration, Nestlé at 14% of 2025 net sales under agreements that run through 2032. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–25, 66–68; calculation D1; calculation D2

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate in aggregate but thinnest in early summer, and two maturity years concentrate the refinancing test. facts.label: Competitive forces, external factors and SWOT
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is high and price-sensitive: the annual report names several large metal container and closure competitors, says Silgan competes on price, quality and service, and notes that customers may self-manufacture, which about 7% of the U.S. metal food container market still does. Buyer power is high because a small number of large food and consumer goods customers hold multi-year contracts with competitive-proposal rights; supplier power is moderate because steel, aluminum and resin come from a limited number of suppliers, offset by pass-through clauses. The threat of new entrants is limited by plant proximity, with metal cans sold mostly within about 300 miles, and substitution by plastic, glass, paper and composite packaging is real outside high-temperature and long-shelf-life food uses. For creditors this means pricing power is limited and earnings depend on volume, mix and contract terms. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 26–27, 31–33

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and diversification are supports: a group of about USD 6.5 billion of sales across three segments, with the largest customer at 14%. Competitive advantage is partial, resting on proximity, contracts and scale rather than pricing power. Cost and capex flexibility is moderate: capital expenditure near USD 310 million a year is not easily cut, though the cost program and plant closures show a lever. Margin stability is good on the three-year record and weaker on the 2026 volume trend. Free cash flow is stable in the annual figure and negative in the seasonal quarters. Access to capital markets has been shown by the September 2025 note sale at par, with no rating supplied. Liquidity is adequate in aggregate and thin in early summer. Financial policy is leverage-for-growth with moderate payouts. The trend is flat: earnings are level, debt is seasonally high, and the transaction adds uncertainty; the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, a rating, pro forma figures and customer contract terms. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 75, 119–120; calculation D3; calculation D7

facts.label: Outlook
facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months management expected higher volumes in dispensing and specialty closures and in metal containers for 2026 and flat custom container volumes, but over nine months of 2026 unit volumes were about 2% lower in dispensing and specialty closures, about 1% lower in metal containers and about 8% lower in custom containers, so the company's own expectation has not been met so far. Tailwinds are pet food growth, prescription dispensing and fragrance volumes, the Europe closure savings and lower interest expense; headwinds are weak beverage closure demand, soup volumes, delayed cost pass-through, tariffs and a higher effective tax rate. Over three to five years the question is whether volume recovery and cost savings, not pass-through pricing, drive earnings, and how the partnership changes the group's debt and ownership. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 20–25

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with a short fruit and vegetable pack combined with weaker pet food and beverage closure volumes in 2027, the pattern of 2024 when severe weather and a large customer's cut in pack plans lowered fixed cost absorption in Metal Containers and group reported EBITDA fell 7.88%. The first operational break is lower plant utilization and delayed pass-through of freight and resin cost; the financial effect is lower EBITDA: applying the 2024 fall to 2025 EBITDA gives about USD 845 million and net leverage of 3.87x on year-end 2025 net debt, and applying it to last-twelve-months EBITDA gives about USD 833 million, net leverage of 5.07x on September 2026 seasonal net debt and cash interest cover near 4.83x. Because a short pack also builds less inventory, operating cash flow rose in 2024 and liquidity was protected, so the strain falls on leverage and refinancing, not on liquidity, as the 2028 notes approach and while the partnership's debt is consolidated. Management levers are the cost program, capital expenditure near USD 310 million, the unused buyback and the USD 2.3 billion distribution. Liquidity appears sufficient to avoid distress; the primary downside path is volume and pass-through pressure that lifts leverage while the 2028 maturities and the transaction compete for the same refinancing window. The 2024 decline also included restructuring and acquisition costs, so it is a bound for an adverse year, not a forecast, and none of these ratios includes the October 19, 2026 announcement, whose pro forma effect on net debt and net leverage is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 62–64, 68, 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D10; calculation D15

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Silgan presents an adequate business profile supported by contract-backed pass-through earnings, steady free cash flow and a record of early refinancing, but credit quality is constrained by seasonal net leverage of 4.67x, flat 2026 earnings, a concentrated 2028 and 2030 maturity profile and a transaction that leaves claim priority open. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because 2025 free cash flow covered distributions 2.63 times and margins held through the 2024 shock. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how the USD 2.3 billion distribution is applied, on market access in 2027 and on the bank group's appetite for the revolver to 2029. The primary downside path is volume and pass-through pressure that lifts leverage while the 2028 maturities and the transaction compete for the same refinancing window. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the executed credit agreement, pro forma net debt and leverage, a rating and customer contract terms. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: leverage and claim priority after the transaction. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D9; calculation D12

## Request

Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway, run slgn-849869-2026-11-18-credit_snapshot-host. Scope: whether the five supplied SEC filings of the registrant (two annual and three quarterly reports) can support the requested Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit work, and what the rest of the pathway would lack. No objective was stated, so the pathway's own question, whether to own this issuer, in which instrument and why, is the objective.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings support financial-statement, debt and business work through the third quarter of 2026, but not covenant, legal-ranking, rating or transaction conclusions, so creditors cannot yet test covenant headroom or claim priority from this source set.

A material open item is the transaction announced on October 19, 2026, which would place the Metal Containers segment in a majority-owned partnership with its own secured debt; the quarterly report describes it in a single note, so the perimeter after closing and any pro forma leverage are not established. The executed credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and dated market quotes are not supplied, and the filings print no covenant levels, so Legal & covenants work cannot run until the documents arrive. Annual figures are audited and interim figures are unaudited.

## Gaps

No executed credit agreement, amendment or indenture is in the source set. The annual report lists them as exhibits and the first-quarter report lists the sixth amendment dated March 6, 2026, but the run settings declare no legal documents, so covenant definitions, baskets, guarantor and security terms and the call and change-of-control terms cannot be read from the governing documents. Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control and Recovery & fulcrum work would rest on filing summaries alone and cannot run until the documents are supplied. This is a material gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 91–96; 10-Q_2026-03-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 25

The filings name two financial covenants, Interest Coverage and Total Net Leverage, and state that the company is in compliance, but print no covenant level, no step-down and no reported ratio. Covenant headroom is therefore not established, and the credit agreement's own definition of Total Net Leverage is not available to compare with any leverage measure built from the statements. This is a material gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

The announcement of October 19, 2026 is described only in one note to the third-quarter report: a partnership with an investment vehicle affiliated with funds managed by American Industrial Partners, the contribution of the Metal Containers segment and the food and beverage flat cap closures business, about USD 2.3 billion of cash to the company intended to retire existing debt, a 60% controlling interest for the company and 40% for the partner, about USD 1.0 billion of partner cash, about USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans and a USD 1.0 billion secured revolver at the partnership, and the proposed acquisition of Trivium Packaging B.V. for about USD 327.5 million in cash plus about USD 3.1 billion of assumed debt, expected to close in mid-2027 subject to regulatory approvals and works council consultation. No agreement, sources and uses, pro forma balance sheet, pro forma leverage or separate figures for the flat cap closures business are supplied, so the perimeter and pro forma net debt after closing are not established, and every figure in the filings is a reported pre-transaction figure that must not be blended with the announcement. This is a material gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

Directors, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and director independence are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the source set; only the signature page names the directors and officers. Governance and ownership assessment in Business & governance is limited to what the business and risk sections state. This is a material gap for that work.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 99

The guarantor perimeter changed inside the period: the subsidiary guarantees of the three senior note series were released on March 31, 2026. Summarized obligor-group figures are printed only as of and for 2025 and 2024, the 2026 reports give none, and the exhibit naming the current subsidiary guarantors and issuers of guaranteed securities is listed but not supplied. Structural priority work cannot rely on the 2025 obligor-group figures for the current guarantor set. This is a material gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 98

No agency credit rating, outlook or rating report appears in any of the five filings or in the run settings, so Ratings & triggers work would have nothing to start from. This is a minor gap for the requested work.

No bond price, yield or spread on a dated trading day is supplied. The third-quarter report prints period-end fair values for the three senior note series, estimated from quoted market prices, which gives a quarter-end price level but not a trade date, yield or spread; Market-implied risk and Security selection work are limited to that. This is a minor gap for the requested work.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10
No portfolio, mandate or exposure data is supplied, so Committee decision work states the fund's limits as not supplied and portfolio fit is not established. This is a minor gap.

The filings define adjusted EBIT, reconciled by segment, but no adjusted EBITDA, no company-defined net leverage, no management guidance, and no earnings release or investor presentation is supplied, so any EBITDA or leverage measure is built by the analyst from the statements and is not a company-reported figure. This is a minor gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66

Stand-alone quarterly reports for 2025 are not supplied. The 2025 quarters are available as comparatives inside the 2026 reports, but the fourth quarter of 2025 exists only as the annual figure less nine months, and no discrete quarter of 2024 can be built because the 2024 interim reports are absent. This is a minor gap.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 102–104

spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation for Silgan Holdings Inc (slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the financial foundation from the five supplied filings, with the FY2023 to FY2025 annual statements, the 2026 interim statements, debt, liquidity and leverage, and the October 19, 2026 subsequent event kept apart from the period figures. No earlier module output other than source readiness was used.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-27 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 30eda6c1d3a71e5756521f79866728a0525f47e4366ea84f392cee9c4faeaa19 | FY2023 balance sheet, FY2024 debt note and obligor group, cross-check of FY2024 comparatives |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 1738ec14e163b7062f9cd82459b8d89a520eca7467d6d8e67e316124174bc20c | FY2023 to FY2025 statements, debt note, maturity ladder, segment note, non-GAAP reconciliation, liquidity |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-06 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 7625ce57afab4b3f5fe74b1c75a7ec19775129e89c9c1d858cdee304020fab1c | First-quarter 2026 and 2025 statements, debt note, revolver availability |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-06 (signature date; filing date not stated) | f89bb14bdf363243a81f33f3e2ac7c8bbd35227b94898782b886a92d65175254 | Second-quarter and half-year statements, debt note, revolver availability |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 (signature date; filing date not stated) | a5cbd60f027db11798a207adadf0751acd94f38d9e18d90fb57c43685f1736cd | Third-quarter and nine-month statements, debt note, liquidity, supply chain finance, subsequent event |
Supplied upstream output: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dea6590f16107f877923b231c0ec26ca6e7c92ecf169979faaaa0597ab3a987a.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage swings with the packing season: 4.67x on last-twelve-months EBITDA at September 30, 2026 and 4.93x at June 30, against 3.56x at year-end 2025, so creditors rely on revolver access until cash rebuilds at year-end.
Basis: calculation C83; calculation C80; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

Cash interest cover is 5.24x on the same last-twelve-months basis, up from 4.95x in FY2025, but the maturity ladder is concentrated in 2028 at 31.89% of principal, and the transaction announced on October 19, 2026 changes the perimeter and debt in ways the filings do not quantify, so its pro forma effect on net debt and leverage is not established.
Basis: calculation C84; calculation C75; calculation C102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Leverage and coverage

Leverage stepped up with the October 2024 purchase of Weener Packaging, paid for with USD 921.563 million of cash and funded by euro term loans and revolver borrowings, and eased in FY2025 as reported EBITDA grew 15.94% to USD 917.030 million. Total debt over EBITDA moved from 3.99x in FY2023 to 5.23x in FY2024 and 4.74x in FY2025, and net debt over EBITDA from 3.24x to 4.19x and 3.56x, so the FY2025 improvement came from earnings growth while total debt itself rose from USD 4,136.853 million to USD 4,346.848 million.

Basis: calculation C67; calculation C70; calculation C73; calculation C68; calculation C71; calculation C74; calculation C85; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 103

On the last-twelve-months basis total debt over EBITDA was 5.07x, 5.31x and 5.03x at the three 2026 quarter ends, and net debt over EBITDA 4.60x, 4.93x and 4.67x. Net debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 335.037 million below net debt at September 30, 2025; the same comparison on leverage is not calculable because nine months of 2024 are not supplied.

Basis: calculation C76; calculation C79; calculation C82; calculation C77; calculation C80; calculation C83; calculation C90; calculation C91; 10-Q_2026-03-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

EBITDA covered cash interest 5.53x in FY2023, 4.94x in FY2024 and 4.95x in FY2025, and 5.24x on the last-twelve-months basis at September 30, 2026. Cash interest paid in the first nine months of 2026 fell 8.61% against the prior-year period, and interest expense fell on lower average borrowings and lower weighted average rates.
Basis: calculation C69; calculation C72; calculation C75; calculation C84; calculation C89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow in FY2025 was USD 729.841 million, 79.59% of reported EBITDA, and free cash flow after capital expenditures of USD 307.092 million was USD 422.749 million, 46.10% of EBITDA. Dividends and share repurchases of USD 160.675 million used 38.01% of that free cash flow, so shareholder returns were covered by free cash flow in FY2025 but not by the interim seasonal cash flows.
Basis: calculation C96; calculation C94; calculation C95; calculation C97; calculation C98; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104

The interim picture is dominated by working capital. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 646.363 million in the first nine months of 2026, USD 82.398 million worse than the prior-year period, because receivables built by USD 188.902 million more, partly offset by inventory releasing cash. Part of the inventory release came from liquidations of older, lower-cost last-in, first-out layers that lowered cost of goods sold by USD 34.0 million in the nine months, 3.76% of last-twelve-months reported EBITDA.
Basis: calculation C92; calculation C93; calculation C108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Liquidity and maturities

At September 30, 2026 cash of USD 324.989 million and the undrawn revolver of USD 665.6 million gave liquidity of USD 990.589 million, 21.78% of total debt, with USD 812.7 million of revolving loans and USD 21.7 million of letters of credit outstanding against a USD 1,500.0 million commitment that matures in November 2029. The issuer says peak seasonal working-capital needs have averaged about USD 600 million, so revolver availability, not cash, is the buffer from summer into autumn.
Basis: calculation C99; calculation C100; calculation C60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 72

The ladder drawn at December 31, 2025 puts USD 1,379.544 million, 31.89%, in 2028 when the two 2028 senior note series fall due, and USD 1,221.976 million, 28.25%, in 2030 when the term loans mature, while 14.52% fell due in 2026, chiefly the USD 500.0 million secured notes that the company repaid on March 31, 2026 with revolver borrowings and cash, so part of the 2026 maturity moved into the revolver. The ladder predates those events and no ladder at September 30, 2026 is printed.
Basis: calculation C61; calculation C102; calculation C103; calculation C101; calculation C115; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Funding float and subsequent event

Supply chain finance is a non-debt funding source carried in accounts payable: supplier invoices in the programme were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026, up 24.94% from USD 385.8 million a year earlier, equal to 10.60% of total debt and 54.54% of trade accounts payable. The bank may end the programme on ten days' notice, so a withdrawal would turn payables into a draw on the revolver.
Basis: calculation C104; calculation C105; calculation C106; calculation C107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28

The transaction announced on October 19, 2026 is a subsequent event and is excluded from every period figure in this analysis. It would move the Metal Containers segment and the food and beverage flat cap closures business into a partnership 60% owned by the company, with about USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans and a USD 1.0 billion secured revolver at the partnership, a cash distribution of about USD 2.3 billion to the company intended to retire debt, and about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt assumed; the effect on consolidated net debt, leverage and the notes' position is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Data quality and definitions

Reported EBITDA is calculated as income before interest and income taxes plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer states no EBITDA, only adjusted EBIT. It therefore sits after USD 76.773 million of last-twelve-months rationalization charges (8.49% of EBITDA) and after USD 10.333 million of Q3 2026 costs attributed to announced acquisitions (1.14% of EBITDA), and it includes the inventory benefit above; none of these is normalised here and the covenant definition of EBITDA is not available.
Basis: calculation C109; calculation C110; calculation C111; calculation C108; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

The derived fourth quarter of 2025 shows a provision for income taxes of USD 35.849 million on income before income taxes of USD 53.385 million, a 67.15% rate, which is calculated rather than reported and not explained in the filings supplied. Debt in every ratio is carrying value, USD 14.072 million below principal at September 30, 2026, and the interim statements are unaudited.
Basis: calculation C112; calculation C113; calculation C114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Contrary evidence

The strongest evidence against reading leverage as stretched is that FY2025 EBITDA covered cash interest 4.95x, net debt at the September 2026 balance sheet date was USD 335.037 million below a year earlier, and liquidity of USD 990.589 million exceeds the seasonal working-capital need the issuer describes. That reading would win if year-end 2026 net leverage returns to the 3.56x of year-end 2025 or lower. It would lose if net leverage stays above 4.67x at year-end 2026, if EBITDA without the inventory benefit and acquisition costs falls materially, or if the announced transaction adds secured debt ahead of the notes; covenant levels, which would settle the question, are not printed.
Basis: calculation C75; calculation C91; calculation C99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

## Gaps

The issuer states no EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated for every period and adjusted EBITDA, the adjusted leverage and cover ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied. This restricts comparison with covenant EBITDA and with issuer-adjusted leverage. Severity: Medium. The action that would close it is the credit agreement definition of EBITDA or an earnings release that states one.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66

Lines the filings print as a dash are Not supplied rather than zero: loss on early extinguishment of debt in the periods without one, equity in earnings of affiliates in FY2023, the purchase of business in FY2023 and FY2025, proceeds from issuance of long-term debt in the nine months of 2026, debt issuance costs in FY2023 and the first half of 2025, and net sales of corporate and eliminations. Interim statements do not print deferred income taxes, the purchase of business or, for the first quarter and half year, proceeds from issuance of long-term debt, so those cells are Not supplied. These cells restrict nothing in the ratios. Severity: Low. No action is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 102–104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4

The balance sheet prints no total liabilities line, so Total Liabilities is calculated from the printed lines and agrees with assets less equity in every column; discrete second- and third-quarter depreciation and amortization is derived by difference because only year-to-date figures are printed; the fourth quarter of 2025 is calculated as the full year less nine months because no fourth quarter is reported. Severity: Low. The fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close the last of these.
Basis: calculation C28; calculation C4; calculation C54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

The 2023 revolver commitment and letters of credit are not printed in the supplied filings, although no revolving loans were outstanding at the end of 2023, so undrawn committed facilities for FY2023 is Not supplied and the liquidity series starts at FY2024. Undrawn committed facilities is the revolver only; other foreign facilities are not quantified. Severity: Medium for the liquidity series. The action is the 2023 annual report and facility-level availability.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

Euro-denominated principal at September 30, 2026 is not printed for the euro term loans, and the filing prints only US dollar translations for the 2028 and 2031 euro notes, so the debt instrument table shows the translations as the amount in the reporting currency, with the euro principal Not supplied for the term loans and taken from the issue amount in the annual report for the notes; no rate is applied. Severity: Low. The action is the 2026 annual report note.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–124

Other foreign bank revolving and term loans and finance leases, together USD 88.978 million, state no ranking or security, so they are left out of the debt stack and the cumulative leverage excludes them. Severity: Low. The action is the underlying loan terms.
Basis: calculation C65; calculation C66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 8

The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025 and predates the 2026 prepayment of USD 42.5 million of term loans and the repayment of the USD 500.0 million secured notes, and no ladder at September 30, 2026 is supplied. Severity: Medium. The action is the 2026 annual report ladder or a lender schedule.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9

Last-twelve-months leverage at September 30, 2025 is not calculable because nine months of 2024 are not supplied, so no year-on-year comparison of trailing leverage at the same seasonal date is possible. Severity: Low. The action is the 2025 quarterly reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 2

The pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on net debt and net leverage is not established: the filing states no net debt effect, no sources and uses and no pro forma balance sheet, and the post-balance-sheet table therefore carries Not supplied figures. Severity: High. The action is the transaction agreements and pro forma financial information.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

Covenant levels, reported covenant ratios and the credit agreement definitions of Total Net Leverage and Interest Coverage are not printed, so covenant headroom cannot be stated and the ratios here are on this module's own definitions. Severity: High for covenant work. The action is the credit agreement and compliance certificates.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27

Funds from operations is not defined in the filings or in the method, so funds from operations over total debt is Not calculable. Severity: Low. The action is an analyst definition agreed with the reader.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104

The annual report discussion prints total adjusted EBIT for FY2023 as 660.5 in millions while the note prints 660,553 in thousands, a rounding difference in the sum of rounded segment figures; the note figure is used. Severity: Low. No action is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144

FY2022 and earlier periods are not carried, although the 2024 annual report prints FY2022 income and cash flow statements, so FY2023 growth rates are Not supplied. Severity: Low. The action is to carry FY2022 if a longer series is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 106

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for Silgan Holdings Inc (slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Silgan Holdings Inc (issuer slgn-849869), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, governance, history and announced-transaction facts that matter to a creditor, from the five supplied filings of the registrant and the source readiness output; leverage, covenant levels, legal ranking and recovery are left to the modules that own them.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-27 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 30eda6c1d3a71e5756521f79866728a0525f47e4366ea84f392cee9c4faeaa19 | Prior-year baseline: facility and country counts, customer concentration for 2022 to 2024, holders of record at January 31, 2025, Weener acquisition description, March 2022 redemption of the 4¾% notes |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 1738ec14e163b7062f9cd82459b8d89a520eca7467d6d8e67e316124174bc20c | Primary source: business, segments, customers, contracts, raw materials, competition, labor, risk factors, governance provisions, dividend and repurchase policy, debt note guarantor and security description, exhibit list, auditor opinions, signatories |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-06 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 7625ce57afab4b3f5fe74b1c75a7ec19775129e89c9c1d858cdee304020fab1c | Checked for events between the annual report and the third quarter: sixth credit agreement amendment, the March 31, 2026 repayment, treasury shares withheld for tax; no subsequent event note |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-08-06 (signature date; filing date not stated) | f89bb14bdf363243a81f33f3e2ac7c8bbd35227b94898782b886a92d65175254 | Checked for interim events, share and dividend data at June 30, 2026; carries no announcement of the October 2026 transactions |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Silgan Holdings Inc. for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 (signature date; filing date not stated) | a5cbd60f027db11798a207adadf0751acd94f38d9e18d90fb57c43685f1736cd | Latest evidence: segment results to September 30, 2026, debt note, supply chain finance, inventory program, treasury stock, stock plan, shares outstanding at October 31, 2026 and the October 19, 2026 subsequent event note |
Supplied upstream output: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 dea6590f16107f877923b231c0ec26ca6e7c92ecf169979faaaa0597ab3a987a.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Silgan is a scaled, contract-anchored packaging issuer, but the announced partnership would move its largest segment by sales into a separately financed structure that outside investors part-own, so creditors cannot yet size claim priority or leverage. Metal Containers produced 48.4% of 2025 net sales and 36.0% of adjusted EBIT, and Silgan would keep a 60% controlling interest and receive about USD 2.3 billion of cash that it intends to use to retire certain existing debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A2

Governance is conventional for a listed company with no sponsor: the supplied filings document no related-party payments, dividends took 29.74% of 2025 net income and the USD 500.0 million buyback authorization was untouched through September 2026. The gap is control: who the larger holders are, and what the founders' stockholders agreement says, sit in documents that are not in the source set.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 90, 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A7
### Key findings

The business is diversified across three packaging segments and anchored by contracts that pass raw-material cost through, which gives creditors more cash-flow visibility than a single-product packager would. Metal Containers was 48.4% of 2025 net sales, Dispensing and Specialty Closures 41.8% and Custom Containers 9.8%; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year arrangements, metal costs pass through by contract and resin costs pass through with a lag in many cases. The other side is a thin metal margin: Metal Containers earned an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025 against 15.5% in Dispensing and Specialty Closures.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 17, 21–22, 66–68; calculation A1

Nestlé is the one material customer concentration, and it is protected by contract rather than removed. Nestlé bought 14% of 2025 consolidated net sales and 13% in 2024 and 2023, and no other customer passed 10%; metal food containers sold to Nestlé were USD 799.8 million, or 12.3% of group sales, under long-term supply agreements that run through 2032 and price by formula. A loss or repricing would fall mainly on Metal Containers, the segment the announced partnership would hold.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 25, 145; calculation A6

Underlying 2026 operating momentum is weaker than the sales line suggests. Nine-month net sales rose 4.6%, mostly from cost pass-through and currency, while unit volumes fell in all three segments and adjusted EBIT was flat at USD 572.2 million against USD 572.6 million. An inventory program liquidated older LIFO layers and cut cost of goods sold by USD 34.0 million in the nine months, USD 26.8 million of it in the third quarter; if the whole benefit sits in adjusted EBIT, the measure would have been 6.01% below the prior-year nine months and 5.97% below the prior-year quarter without it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15–16, 18–20, 22–23; calculation A13; calculation A14

The announced perimeter takes the largest segment by sales, and a large share of earnings, out of the direct reach of Silgan's existing creditors. Metal Containers contributed 36.0% of 2025 adjusted EBIT and 38.60% in the first nine months of 2026, and the perimeter also includes a flat cap closures business whose size is not stated. Silgan would own 60% of the partnership and consolidate it, but the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and USD 1.0 billion secured revolver would be secured by the partnership's assets only, and the other 40% would belong to an investment vehicle affiliated with American Industrial Partners that contributes about USD 1.0 billion of cash. Unless existing guarantees and share pledges continue to cover the contributed subsidiaries, which the note does not say, existing creditors of the parent would reach those assets only through the 60% interest, after the partnership's own lenders. The partnership would also buy Trivium, which the 2025 annual report names among the most significant metal container competitors, so the combination adds scale in the segment that already carries the largest customer concentration and depends on regulatory approval.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation A2; calculation A3

The senior notes now rest on the parent alone while the bank debt keeps subsidiary support. The U.S. subsidiaries' guarantees of the three unsecured senior note series, USD 1,849.38 million of principal and 40.54% of total debt at September 30, 2026, fell away automatically on March 31, 2026 when the secured 1.4% notes were repaid, and the filings print no replacement guarantor. The Credit Agreement, 57.51% of debt principal, stays guaranteed by the U.S. subsidiaries and a Dutch borrower subsidiary and is supported by pledges of subsidiary shares, so noteholders sit behind subsidiary-level claims, and the partnership's secured lenders would add another layer ahead of them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 118, 122–124; calculation A10

Management states that it uses leverage to fund growth and shareholder returns, and the 2024 to 2026 record matches that policy. Weener Packaging cost USD 921.6 million net of cash acquired in October 2024 and was financed with euro loans and cash; dividends have risen every year since 2004; cash returned through dividends and repurchases was 80.65% of net income in 2023, 33.06% in 2024, 55.71% in 2025 and 30.82% in the first nine months of 2026; interest and other debt expense absorbed 31.7% of 2025 income before interest and taxes. The planned USD 2.3 billion debt retirement would be creditor-supportive if completed, but the same announcement adds about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt to be assumed, so the net effect on consolidated debt is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 55, 59–60, 75, 109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16; calculation A8; calculation A9; calculation A12

Working capital leans on bank-run programs, which is funding that is not counted as debt. Customer-based supply chain finance programs covered about 16% of net sales in 2025 and 2024 and improved days sales outstanding by about 28 days, and supplier invoices in the supplier program were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 385.8 million a year earlier, up 24.94%. If the programs ended, net working capital would rise and the revolver would fund it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation A16

Governance is conventional and the audit record is clean, but the control picture is incomplete. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named; the company had 20 holders of record at January 31, 2026; the board is classified and fixed at seven seats subject to a temporary increase, while nine directors signed the annual report; the chair and the chief executive are different people; the auditor has served since 1987 and gave unqualified opinions, including on internal control; and no restatement, waiver or going-concern statement appears. Director independence, compensation, beneficial ownership and related-party transactions are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement is listed but not supplied, so the sponsor and governance risk read is medium and provisional.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 51, 55, 88–90, 98–101; calculation A17
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the announced transaction, if completed as described, would pay down about half of the group's debt: the USD 2.3 billion cash distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, and Silgan would keep control and full consolidation of the segment. The operating base also has a resilient record: multi-year contracts covered about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales, the USD 50 million cost program was completed with about USD 20 million of savings in 2024 and about USD 30 million in 2025, adjusted EBIT rose to USD 723.3 million in 2025 from USD 658.2 million, and the supplied filings show no covenant waiver, restatement, related-party payment or exchange offer.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 24, 66; calculation A11

Executed agreements and a pro forma capital structure would settle the largest open question: which debt is retired, whether the Trivium debt is refinanced or stays in place, and whether the partnership's lenders have any recourse to Silgan. Which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or unsecured notes. Evidence of a large founder or fund holder, or terms in the 2022 stockholders agreement that bind the board, would move the governance read from conventional to influenced. A debt-funded dividend or repurchase after the transaction, loss or repricing of the Nestlé agreement, or a second year of volume declines without pass-through offsets would move the view the other way.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 98
### Limitations

- The October 2026 announcement is described in one note with no executed agreements, sources and uses or pro forma balance sheet, so the conclusions on claim priority, perimeter and debt after closing are directional and rest on pre-transaction figures.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

- The proxy statement, the Schedule 13G holder names and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement are not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the absence of a named sponsor and would change if a founder or fund holds a large block.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 90, 98

- Only segment sales, adjusted EBIT, depreciation, assets and capital expenditure are printed by segment, so the share of group cash flow that would sit in the partnership is approximated by its adjusted EBIT share and could differ materially.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Customer contracts are not supplied, so the revenue durability conclusion rests on management's statements of contract coverage and the Nestlé end date, and renewal, termination or volume commitments could be weaker than stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 25

- Statements that the company is a leader or has more than half of the U.S. metal food container market are management's and are not tested against independent market data, so the competitive position conclusion is management's view.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 17
- The nine-month 2026 figures are unaudited and the inventory benefit is stated only for the group, so the underlying earnings estimate changes if part of that benefit sits outside adjusted EBIT.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On October 19, 2026 Silgan announced agreements to create a partnership, Silgan MCC, with an investment vehicle affiliated with funds managed by American Industrial Partners. Silgan would contribute its Metal Containers segment and its food and beverage flat cap closures business and would receive about USD 2.3 billion of cash, which it intends to use to retire certain existing debt, and a 60% controlling ownership interest; the investment vehicle would contribute about USD 1.0 billion of cash for 40%. The partnership would have an independent balance sheet that is fully consolidated into Silgan's statements and would be financed by about USD 4.9 billion of new senior secured term loans and a new senior secured revolving facility of USD 1.0 billion, which the company describes as fully committed and secured by assets of the partnership only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16

The partnership would also acquire Trivium Packaging B.V., a Netherlands supplier of metal packaging, for a cash payment of about USD 327.5 million and the assumption of about USD 3.1 billion of Trivium's debt. Trivium is one of the competitors that the 2025 annual report names among the most significant in metal containers. Closing is expected in mid-2027 and is subject to regulatory approvals, works council consultation and customary conditions. Costs attributed to announced acquisitions were USD 10.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, against USD 1.1 million in the first nine months of 2025, and adjusted EBIT excludes them; the filing does not tie them to a named transaction. The note gives no agreement terms, no sources and uses, no pro forma balance sheet and no separate figures for the flat cap closures business; the stated cash sources of USD 5.9 billion exceed the stated cash uses of USD 2.3 billion to Silgan and USD 327.5 million to Trivium's sellers by about USD 3.27 billion, close to the USD 3.1 billion of Trivium debt, which is consistent with refinancing that debt but does not establish it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 19–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation A12

Silgan issued no notes or term loans in the first nine months of 2026. The last new issue was EUR 600.0 million of senior notes due 2031, sold at par on September 12, 2025 and used to repay euro revolving loans that had funded the March 15, 2025 repayment of EUR 650.0 million of senior notes. In 2026 Silgan prepaid USD 42.5 million of U.S. term loans on February 3, amended the Credit Agreement on March 6 to improve term loan pricing, and on March 31 repaid all USD 500.0 million of its 1.4% secured notes with revolving loans and cash, which released the subsidiary guarantees of the other three note series.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120, 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 9

The stated cash sources exceed the stated cash uses by about USD 3.27 billion, which is close to the Trivium debt but is not explained. This is a material gap for the corporate structure and claim priority conclusions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation A12

Ownership detail is missing. The proxy statement, the names of holders of 10% or more, director and officer ownership and the 2022 founders' stockholders agreement are not in the source set, so the conclusion that the company has no controlling holder rests on the absence of a named sponsor. This is a material gap for the governance read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 90, 98

Customer contracts, including the Nestlé agreements that run through 2032, are not supplied, so price formulas, termination rights and volume commitments cannot be read. This is a minor gap for the revenue durability conclusion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 25

Weener Packaging results are not shown separately after the October 2024 acquisition, so its contribution to the 17.5% growth in dispensing and specialty closures sales in 2025 cannot be separated from organic growth. This is a minor gap for the acquisition integration evidence.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 67

The ownership percentages of the three joint ventures and the lists of subsidiaries and guarantors after the March 31, 2026 release are exhibits that are not supplied. This is a minor gap for the ownership map.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24, 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9
No agency credit rating or outlook is stated in any supplied filing or in the run settings. This is a minor gap.

Segment-level debt, cash flow and working capital are not printed, so the cash flow that would sit in the partnership is approximated by adjusted EBIT share only. This is a minor gap for the perimeter conclusion.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 15

The company's statements that it is a leader in each business and holds more than half of the U.S. metal food container market are not tested against independent market data, and the estimate of the market still served by self-manufacturers moved from about 6% in the 2024 annual report to about 7% in the 2025 annual report. This is a minor gap for the competitive position conclusion.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11

## Findings
### Bottom line

Silgan's fundamental credit profile is adequate: contract-backed cash flows and steady free cash flow support the debt, but flat 2026 earnings, seasonal net leverage of 4.67x and an unquantified October 2026 transaction leave creditors with less cushion than year-end figures suggest.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D8

Free cash flow of about USD 423 million covered 2025 dividends and buybacks 2.63 times, and liquidity of about USD 991 million at September 30, 2026 exceeds the roughly USD 600 million seasonal need the company cites. Net leverage was 3.56x at year-end 2025; the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on net debt and net leverage is not established. About 60.14% of principal falls due in 2028 and 2030, so how the transaction retires debt will shape the refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 27; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D7; calculation D9
### Key findings

The business supports the debt through contract-backed, cost-pass-through earnings rather than growth. Reported EBITDA margins stayed between 13.51% and 14.34% from 2023 to 2025 even though EBITDA fell 7.88% in 2024; about 90% of projected 2026 metal container sales sit under multi-year contracts that pass metal cost through, while resin cost passes through with a lag. The price is thin metal margins, an adjusted EBIT margin of 8.3% in 2025, and one concentration, Nestlé at 14% of 2025 net sales under agreements that run through 2032.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 17, 21–25, 66–68; calculation D1; calculation D2

Free cash flow covers distributions but has not reduced debt. Free cash flow after capital expenditure was about USD 423 million in 2025, 46.10% of reported EBITDA, and covered dividends and buybacks 2.63 times; yet net debt fell only USD 47.81 million and total debt rose, so the improvement in leverage came from EBITDA growth, not repayment. Free cash flow after shareholder returns was about USD 262 million, a pace that would not shrink net debt quickly against a seasonal swing of the size seen in 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 103–104; calculation D3; calculation D4; calculation D5

Leverage is elevated at the seasonal peak and the 2026 earnings trend does not help. Net debt over reported EBITDA was 3.56x at year-end 2025, and the pro forma effect of the October 19, 2026 announcement on that figure is not established; it was 4.67x at September 30, 2026 on last-twelve-months EBITDA, with total debt at 5.03x. Last-twelve-months EBITDA of about USD 904 million is 1.44% below 2025, and it would be a further 3.76% lower, with net leverage at 4.85x, without the USD 34.0 million inventory benefit.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 15, 18–20; calculation D2; calculation D6; calculation D10

Liquidity is adequate in aggregate but thinnest in early summer, and two maturity years concentrate the refinancing test. Cash plus revolver availability was about USD 991 million at September 30, 2026 but about USD 754 million at June 30, when revolver availability of USD 402.4 million was below the USD 600 million seasonal need; the USD 1,500.0 million revolver matures in November 2029. At December 31, 2025, 31.89% of principal fell due in 2028 and 28.25% in 2030, together 60.14%.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73, 114; calculation D7; calculation D9

The October 2026 transaction is the swing factor for claim priority and leverage, and the filings do not let a creditor size it. The USD 2.3 billion distribution equals 50.42% of total debt principal at September 30, 2026, 124.37% of the unsecured senior notes and 87.66% of Credit Agreement debt, so which instruments are retired decides whether the remaining parent claims are mostly secured bank debt or mostly unsecured notes; the partnership's USD 4.9 billion of new secured term loans rank on its own assets only, and the Trivium acquisition is expected to close in mid-2027, ahead of the 2028 note maturities.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D12

Funding that does not show as debt deepens reliance on banks. Supplier invoices in the supply chain finance program were USD 482.0 million at September 30, 2026, up 24.94% in a year and equal to 10.60% of total debt, and customer programs covered about 16% of net sales; the bank can end the supplier program on short notice, which would turn payables into revolver draws at the point of seasonal peak.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 27–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D13

Financial policy and governance are a moderate risk rather than a decisive one. Dividends took 29.74% of 2025 net income and the USD 500.0 million buyback authorization was unused in the first nine months of 2026, but management states that it uses leverage to fund growth and shareholder returns, interest and other debt expense absorbed 31.7% of 2025 income before interest and taxes, and ownership detail sits in documents that are not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 13; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that net debt at September 30, 2026 was about USD 335 million, 7.35%, below the same date a year earlier, last-twelve-months EBITDA covered cash interest 5.24x, the revolver runs to November 2029, and Silgan sold EUR 600.0 million of notes at par in September 2025. The announced distribution would also retire about half of total debt principal if applied as intended, and the 2024 pack shortfall showed that a weak packing year cut earnings but raised operating cash flow, partly because inventory built less.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; calculation D11; calculation D12

Year-end 2026 net leverage at or below the 3.56x of year-end 2025, a level whose pro forma effect from the October 19, 2026 announcement is not established, a pro forma capital structure that shows net leverage below that level after closing, early refinancing of the 2028 notes and a return of unit volume growth would improve the view. Year-end 2026 net leverage above the 4.67x of September 30, 2026, revolver availability below the USD 600 million seasonal need at the 2027 low, a distribution that retires secured bank debt while leaving the notes behind new secured debt, or a revolver-funded buyback would worsen it. Covenant levels, which would settle the headroom question, are not printed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 27; calculation D7; calculation D12
### Limitations

- Covenant levels and the credit agreement's own definition of leverage are not printed, so the conclusion that leverage and liquidity are adequate rests on trend and cash cover and cannot be tested against headroom.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 76, 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 27
- No rating, dated bond quote or peer figure is supplied, so the adequate reading is an absolute view built on the issuer's own history, not a ranking against sector peers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- EBITDA is calculated as income before interest and taxes plus depreciation and amortization, after restructuring and acquisition costs and including the inventory benefit, because the company states no EBITDA, so every leverage ratio moves with that choice.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66
- Pro forma net debt, leverage and the instruments to be retired are not stated, so the refinancing and leverage conclusions describe the pre-transaction group only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The maturity ladder is printed only at December 31, 2025 and predates the March 2026 repayment and prepayment, and no year-end 2026 estimate exists, so the maturity concentration is an approximation and the outlook and downside are qualitative.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_slgn.htm.jsonl, page 9
